pages.x: Yemen, the poorest country in the Arab world, had been ruled for 33 years by Ali Abdullah Saleh, until protests in 2011 forced him to hand power to his deputy, Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi. The new government was weak, and in the mountains of the north a Zaydi Shia rebel movement, the Houthis, was growing strong.

In September 2014 Houthi fighters, now allied with their old enemy Saleh, marched into the capital, Sanaa. In early 2015 they put President Hadi under house arrest. He escaped to Aden, and as the Houthis closed in on the city, fled to Saudi Arabia.

On 26 March 2015 Saudi Arabia, which saw the Houthis as the tool of its rival Iran, led a coalition of Arab states into the war, with air strikes and a blockade. Its young defence minister, Mohammed bin Salman, hoped for a quick victory. The United States and Britain sold the coalition weapons and helped it.

Forces backed by the United Arab Emirates drove the Houthis out of Aden in 2015, but then the front lines barely moved. Coalition air strikes hit weddings, funerals, markets and, in 2018, a school bus, while Houthi shells and missiles struck Yemeni towns and Saudi cities. In 2017 Saleh broke with the Houthis, and they killed him.

The war, the blockade and the collapse of the economy brought Yemen to the edge of famine, and the UN called it the world's worst humanitarian crisis. Millions lived on food aid, and from 2016 one of the largest cholera outbreaks ever recorded spread through the country.

In 2018 coalition-backed forces fought to take Hodeidah, the port through which most of Yemen's food arrived, until a deal brokered by the UN in Stockholm stopped them. From 2020 the Houthis threw wave after wave of fighters at Marib, the government's last stronghold in the north, but could not take it.

In April 2022 a truce brokered by the UN paused the air strikes and the big offensives, and Hadi handed power to a council of leaders. The truce ran out in October, but the large-scale fighting did not return, and Saudi Arabia began talking directly to the Houthis.

From late 2023, saying they acted in support of Gaza, the Houthis fired missiles at Israel and attacked merchant ships in the Red Sea, and many ships went the long way around Africa. The United States, Britain and Israel struck back with air raids. In May 2025 the United States and the Houthis agreed a ceasefire.

By 2025 the war had killed hundreds of thousands of people, more of them through hunger and disease than in the fighting. Yemen was still divided, between the Houthis in the north and the government and its rival allies in the south, and no peace had been signed.
pts: One of the worst humanitarian crises of its time
